flagged.evidence: The title calls this “A uniformly gapped occupied-projector response map,” but the Definition sets Φ(X) whenever the gap at that individual X is strict; its separate uniform-gap clause requires a common g>0 only for every X in a set K. The in-scope example H(t)=diag(-t,t) has Φ defined for all t∈(0,1], although the gaps 2t have infimum 0 on that set. Thus the title overstates the domain condition defined.

The page says the map is defined “only where a uniform occupied/unoccupied spectral gap” holds. The Definition requires only a strict gap at each point where Φ is evaluated and defines a uniform gap separately for a set. In the in-scope example H(t)=diag(-t,t), Φ is defined for every t∈(0,1], but no common positive gap holds on that set.

The title says relaxed mixing contracts “only under a uniform derivative bound,” asserting necessity. Counterexample: take K={P0} with P0=diag(1,0), U=H₂, F(D)=diag(0,1), and α=0. Then Φ(P0)=P0 and T₀ restricted to K is a contraction with factor 0, while DT₀(P0)=I has induced Frobenius norm 1, so no uniform derivative bound q<1 holds.

The page says the examples “add an eigensolver error to the residual certificate.” The in-scope additive-tolerance example explicitly says it “is not itself an eigensolve”; it supplies a computed response value and certified response-evaluation error η=1/100. The calculation adds response-evaluation error by the triangle inequality, not an eigensolver error.
